Hi Jonas,

We ran a short internal projection for our chat-based product and want to validate whether a Redwood Dedicated pool is the right approach. High level:
- Steady-state: ~1,200 requests / minute (peak 2x for 30 minutes/day)
- Average prompt + response tokens: 1,200 tokens round-trip (avg context ~1,000)
- Target p95 latency: <250ms for short responses; p99 SLO for 3s
- Concurrency: expected 210 concurrent sessions during peak window
- Model: planning to run an Llama2-70B-v2 4-bit variant (quantized)

Can you give a right-size recommendation for GPU count and any throughput guarantees we should consider for a 12-month reserved commit? Also, what discount bands do you typically offer for 12/24 month commits?

Attaching a small export from our load tests.

Samantha — thanks for the details and the CSV. I took a quick pass and have a few clarifying questions, plus an initial right-size sketch below.

Questions:
- Is the 1,200 rpm uniformly distributed across requests, or do you see regional spikes? (helps with routing/replication)
- Are the 210 concurrent sessions long-lived (minutes) or short bursts (seconds)?

Initial right-size (very conservative):
- Model: Llama2-70B-v2 q4_0 (4-bit) — validated in our infra for good perf/cost tradeoff.
- Baseline throughput per A100-like GPU (mixed; benchmarked with your 1,200 token avg): ~18–22 requests/sec (approx) assuming continuous batching + KV cache for prefixes.
- For peak concurrency (210 sessions) and your token lengths, we recommend starting with 12 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) with a plan to scale to 16 during 2x peak windows. That gives headroom for autoscale and rolling updates.

Commit & SLA framing to consider:
- 12-month reserved commit (monthly billing) with a baseline throughput SLA (tokens/sec aggregated) rather than strict per-request p95 guarantees — allows us to give a meaningful discount while retaining burst capacity.
- For p99 SLOs on individual short responses we recommend layering small burst capacity (2–4 GPUs) or using our hosted fallback model for sub-250ms needs.

I can put figures and a pricing band together — looping in Marissa to outline discount bands and Laura for procurement coordination.

— Jonas

Samantha — great to meet you over email. Jonas' sketch is aligned with our benchmarks. A couple of commercial notes before we finalize: 

Discounting: typical bands we offer for Dedicated reserved commits (baseline guidance):
- 12-month: 10–18% off list for mid-market commits (~$X/month baseline)
- 24-month: 18–28% for larger commits with guaranteed throughput and a minimum FTE support add-on
- Additional volume/usage credits can move you into the next band; we usually structure an explicit throughput metric in the SOW.

Right-sizing cadence: we usually start with a conservative commit (12 GPUs equivalent) and include one scheduled review at 90 days to validate telemetry and adjust commit/credits.

Attached is our standard reserved commit term sheet (v1) and a short worksheet we use for the right-size call.

Procurement — thanks for the clear asks. Below is an actionable proposal you can share with legal/finance; I kept this intentionally specific so it maps cleanly to SOW line items.

Summary recommendation (finalized):
- Baseline commit: 12 GPU equivalents (A100-class) dedicated pool configured for Llama2-70B-v2 q4_0.
- Peak scaling: policy to autoscale up to 16 GPUs for bursts (2x peak windows). Autoscale billing will charge at committed rate up to 10% burst capacity; additional burst hours billed at overage rate.
- Throughput SLA: aggregate tokens/sec SLA of 1,000,000 tokens/min (monthly aggregated) mapped to credits. If monthly aggregated throughput falls below 95% of committed tokens, we issue pro-rata credits on the subsequent invoice.
- Latency SLOs: we provide p95 latency target of 300ms for responses under 800 tokens in the committed pool; for strict sub-250ms p95 we recommend a hybrid approach (small hosted fallback pool for the 5% lowest-latency traffic).
- Under-utilization policy: 60-day review window. If utilization <55% across two consecutive months, we offer either (a) one-time re-baseline credit equal to 10% of that quarter's committed fee, or (b) an option to downscale pool size at the next billing cycle with a 30-day notice and adjusted discount band.

Pricing (indicative) — for contracting purposes only:
- Committed monthly baseline (12 GPUs): $XXX,XXX / month (list-equivalent $YYY,YYY); 12-month term at 14% discount applied to list.
- Autoscale buffer (up to 16 GPUs): included up to 10% of monthly hours; excess billed at overage rate $ZZZ/hour per GPU-equivalent.
- One scheduled health & right-size review at 90 days included. Additional SRE on-call add-on available.

Attachments: right-size workbook with estimated token/hour math and the contract-friendly line items.

[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_rightsize.xlsx (XLSX, 56 KB)]

Next steps:
1) If this aligns, Marissa will open a quote and Laura will coordinate SOW items + compliance language around audit logs/data residency.
2) We can schedule a 30m technical review with Marcus to validate benchmarking and runtime knobs (quantization, batching, KV cache TTL).
